text:
Google announced on March 18, 2025 that it had agreed to acquire cloud-security firm Wiz for approximately $32 billion in an all-cash deal [Source: ev-1]. This transaction represented the largest acquisition in Google's history and followed Wiz’s rejection of a previous offer from Google worth $23 billion in July 2024 [Source: ev-1].

The primary motivation for the acquisition was strategic; under Thomas Kurian, Google Cloud sought to close its security gap with competitors AWS and Azure by pursuing consolidation in the cloud-security sector [Source: ev-1]. The move signaled that cloud-security is becoming the next battleground in the "cloud wars," driven largely by AI-driven cloud adoption acting as the key demand driver [Source: ev-1]. While the deal closed after shareholder and regulatory steps were completed—reported in July 2025—the initial announcement occurred in March 2025 [Source: ev-1].
